4c03191b81bb: If differences between the two sides of your face concern you, start by understanding the changes. This guide explains possible causes, symptoms and points to discuss during an assessment.
d88f5b9a7dee: Facial asymmetry is a difference in size, shape, height or position between the two sides of the face.
802dda37825f: Mild differences between the two sides are common. Having facial asymmetry does not, by itself, mean that treatment is needed.
03756ceb24ea: Example of a jaw shifted to one side
fdc23ad531da: Enlarge the facial asymmetry comparison illustration (new window)
ee6470eb97be: Conceptual illustration showing a skull with aligned midlines on the left and a comparison of jaw position using a gray reference line and an angled orange line on the right
baceedda117b: Comparing the facial midline and jaw position
b1e8098c6bbb: In the illustration on the right, the gray dashed line is the reference, while the orange dashed line shows the direction of the jaw's tilt.
64288dff2e3f: This simplified conceptual illustration emphasizes differences in position and tilt. It does not depict an actual patient or before-and-after treatment results, and cannot be used as a diagnostic standard.
d9ae666f6016: Asymmetry may be limited to one area of the face or appear in several areas at once. For example, eyebrow heights may differ while the chin remains centered. Alternatively, the chin may shift to one side while the midlines of the lips and teeth also appear different.
4afc6e8f8cfb: Areas considered when assessing facial asymmetry
32abc3be3e1d: Assessment considers eyebrow height, eyelid shape and differences in soft tissue around the eyes. Eyes that appear different in size are not necessarily caused by structural differences in the eye sockets or skull.
279a0ea9955a: 2. Alignment of the nose and midface
76eee8964197: Assessment considers the direction of the nose, the surrounding contours, and the prominence of the cheekbones and cheeks. Nasal asymmetry and skeletal differences in the midface should be assessed separately.
0ee0713469a2: 3. Position of the lips and mouth corners
4b41362739c9: The heights of the mouth corners may differ at rest and when smiling. Several factors can be involved, including movement of the muscles around the lips, the bite and jaw position.
2719f2da4af4: The chin may appear shifted to one side, or one jaw angle may look more prominent. Assessment should distinguish differences in the shape of the jawbone from those related to lower-jaw position or movement.
81048615698d: The midlines of the upper and lower front teeth may not align, or the lower jaw may move to one side during chewing. It is important to assess tooth alignment, the bite and jaw movement together.
3eede88d9892: Facial asymmetry often cannot be explained by a single cause. Assessment begins by distinguishing differences in appearance from actual functional difficulties.
477dcc2fa3ec: Differences in appearance and functional discomfort should be considered together. This page provides general health information; an examination is needed to assess your individual causes and whether treatment is necessary.
1fed5211e5db: Facial asymmetry may be associated with various factors, including skeletal development, teeth and the bite, jaw joints and chewing muscles, and soft tissue.
98ba04463ba3: Facial bones develop during growth, and the two sides may not grow to exactly the same extent.
6550e9c286d7: Differences in the size or position of the upper and lower jaws, chin deviation and differences between the two jaw angles may contribute to asymmetric facial contours.
44015b08d4b5: In these cases, assessment should consider the shape and position of the jawbones and how the teeth fit together, rather than the facial surface alone. If skeletal asymmetry is suspected, assessment by an orthodontist or an oral and maxillofacial surgeon may be needed.
1a7c5399dbdb: 2. Differences in tooth alignment and the bite
1535bd6d6b26: The alignment of the teeth and the way the upper and lower teeth fit together may affect the position and movement of the lower jaw.
ea3dd0f6bbac: For example, if the bite differs between the two sides or the lower jaw shifts to one side when the teeth meet, facial alignment may appear different when closing the mouth or chewing.
092510169ff3: However, a mismatch between dental midlines alone does not establish asymmetry of the jawbones themselves. Tooth alignment and the structural position of the jaw should be assessed separately.
c016e3b7e102: 3. Functional differences in the jaw joints and chewing muscles
f6d6a023546f: The jaw joints allow the lower jaw to move, while the surrounding chewing muscles are involved in functions such as chewing and opening the mouth.
ae502f815982: If there is jaw-joint pain, restricted movement, deviation when opening the mouth or differences in chewing-muscle tension, facial movement and discomfort around the jaw can be assessed together.
3693a41c74d0: However, a temporomandibular disorder does not necessarily cause facial asymmetry, and jaw-joint symptoms alone cannot establish structural changes in the facial bones.
8eed0b5fb513: 4. Differences in soft tissue and muscles
5215c719e9c6: Facial contours are influenced not only by bone but also by soft tissue, including skin, subcutaneous fat and muscles.
c75b6065e416: Differences in cheek volume, development of the chewing muscles, and skin or subcutaneous tissue may make the two sides of the face look different.
db6798dea7e4: In these cases, it is important to distinguish skeletal differences from differences in appearance arising from soft tissue.
79c6b40319d1: Assessment may also include a history of injury to the face or jaw, changes following dental treatment and conditions affecting the jaw-joint area.
8f4ef1199513: If previously subtle asymmetry becomes more noticeable over time, or the size or shape of one side of the face changes, the cause should be assessed rather than treating it solely as a cosmetic concern.
001a488e38de: Habits such as chewing on one side, clenching the teeth, sleeping position, and neck and shoulder tension can be considered when assessing strain on the jaw and surrounding muscles.
ec45b62d87ab: However, a particular posture or habit alone does not establish that the facial bones have become misaligned. Managing daily habits and assessing the causes of actual skeletal asymmetry should be approached separately.
d9bcf3137475: Consider facial differences alongside any discomfort
07c8559d85e9: Facial asymmetry can be described in several ways, depending on the areas involved and whether differences are more noticeable at rest or during movement.
b86adcca17c0: The categories below are explanations to aid understanding. They are not a standardized diagnostic system that assigns every patient to one specific type.
700faaf53525: The center of the lower jaw or the chin appears shifted to one side of the facial midline.

cadc3a70aa76: With this pattern, the shape and position of the lower jawbone, the bite and jaw-joint movement should be assessed separately.
edcb5791fd2f: Type B. Asymmetry of the mouth corners or smile
ab35355937cd: Differences may be subtle at rest, but one mouth corner rises higher or the lips move differently when smiling or speaking.
84ee21899ddf: One corner of the mouth appears higher
9673c4b27365: The center of the lips shifts to one side when smiling

9fa1bb39e589: These differences may involve several factors, including facial-muscle movement, the teeth and bite, and jaw position. The cause cannot be determined from mouth-corner height alone.
46c570aca0fa: Type C. Cheekbone and midface asymmetry
0ed5eaf872ea: The prominence of the cheekbones, cheek volume or contours around the nose differ between the two sides.
61e40ccfe75a: Cheek volume or contours appear different on the two sides
bac6dfda5066: The left and right sides of the midface appear different in width
c92ca189dd7c: The center of the face appears shifted to one side in frontal photos
e20094545d9c: Differences in skeletal shape and soft tissue can look similar from the outside, so they need to be distinguished.
81fec6a20f27: Type D. Eyebrow and eye-area asymmetry
8f1a75fdc328: Differences in eyebrow height, eyelid shape or soft tissue around the eyes make the eyes appear different in size or level.
8586925e0926: A difference in apparent eye size does not necessarily mean skull asymmetry. Eyelid changes and eye-related causes should also be considered.
c369de56e13e: Asymmetry is observed in several areas at once, such as chin deviation, differences in mouth-corner height and cheekbone prominence.
c421ddbca946: In these cases, the appearance of a single area cannot easily explain the causes affecting the whole face. It is important to assess the skeleton, bite, jaw movement and soft tissue separately.

286d9469afb2: What is assessed during a facial asymmetry consultation?
16faed21291f: Assessment of facial asymmetry considers not only visible differences between the two sides but also when changes appeared, jaw function, the bite and accompanying symptoms.
c0fae9cbf812: The following are general assessment items. For the scope of consultations at Remedi, see
5be46e2f01c9: Step 1. Review when changes began and how they developed
0fe22130a5b9: Assessment includes when the differences between the two sides first concerned you and whether they have been present since childhood or appeared recently.
762c8cdea2ab: A history of injuries, dental treatment and jaw-joint symptoms is also reviewed. Earlier photographs, if available, may help in understanding the pattern of changes.
0168d6d3eaf9: Step 2. Observe the shape of both sides of the face
fdcccde6060d: Assessment observes differences in key areas, including the eyebrows and eye area, nose, cheekbones, mouth corners, chin and jawline.
c1ec66df4591: Where needed, assessment may include differences during movements such as smiling or opening the mouth, as well as the face at rest.
c5972beeca62: Photographs can be used as observation records, but apparent differences may vary with the camera angle, facial expression and lens distortion. Photos alone therefore do not establish a cause.
1c4385d0e723: Step 3. Assess jaw movement and chewing function
aed707f3df38: Assessment considers opening and closing the mouth, jaw deviation, discomfort during chewing and pain around the jaw joints.
1df104affc18: When appropriate, chewing-muscle tension and tenderness, and neck and shoulder discomfort may also be assessed. These findings alone, however, cannot diagnose structural skeletal asymmetry.
ce59008db520: Step 4. Distinguish bite-related and structural concerns
9fc7d7e1f0fe: Assessment determines whether differences in dental midlines and the bite, or the shape and position of the jawbones, require further evaluation.
653ccf4ff5b9: If skeletal asymmetry or problems with tooth alignment or the bite are suspected, assessment by an orthodontist or an oral and maxillofacial surgeon may be needed. Imaging is determined by clinical need rather than performed routinely for every patient.
e3906679281d: Assessment distinguishes concerns about facial appearance from functional discomfort, such as jaw movement or pain, and explains what can be evaluated in your current condition.
c333de4a737d: Even when seeking an improvement in appearance, it is important to clarify what can be targeted, what changes may be difficult to achieve and whether further assessment is needed.
bb292115a00a: How do approaches to facial asymmetry treatment differ?
b6c8e4bd1564: Treatment for facial asymmetry depends on its causes and the goals of care. Improving facial appearance and managing jaw-joint pain or function are different treatment goals.
d1afd858f8ba: If differences are mild and cause no discomfort
3a2faef223ed: Specific treatment may not be necessary if there are no significant concerns about appearance or function. Decisions about treatment consider the cause and the discomfort you experience.
616e6c535f4d: If there is functional discomfort in the jaw joints or chewing muscles
4e32402615da: If there is pain around the jaw joints, difficulty opening the mouth or chewing-muscle tension, the cause of those symptoms can be assessed and conservative care considered.
53998ef63158: Changes to daily habits, appropriate exercises and physical approaches to care may be considered according to the symptoms. This does not mean that such care corrects skeletal facial asymmetry.
69ecd902383b: If skeletal or bite-related differences are suspected
52e260fc5cfb: Suspected differences in jawbone size or position, or problems with the way the teeth fit together, may require structural assessment by an orthodontist or an oral and maxillofacial surgeon.
c8d3a08f0df8: Treatment options are determined by considering the cause and degree of asymmetry, stage of growth and functional problems. Not all asymmetry requires orthodontic treatment or surgery.
5c65c8ab5cfa: If soft-tissue differences and appearance are your main concerns
60b0b109cc67: If your main concern is facial volume, muscle shape or differences in soft tissue between the two sides, the characteristics and causes affecting those areas should be assessed first.
648650658f51: The range of changes that can be expected varies by treatment method. Managing soft-tissue differences is not the same as treatment that changes skeletal shape.
b8bff3b4e90d: About cranial correction and oral appliances
de339655f6f6: Cranial orthoses and corrective appliances should be distinguished according to who they are intended for and their purpose.
